title: 37°C heat shock survival assay for C. elegans
author: Emily Troemel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v6re9d6

steps.title: Pre‑culture worms for assay
steps.instruction: Grow worms without starvation or bleaching for at least three generations at 20 °C before starting the assay.

steps.title: Transfer 30 L4 worms per plate
steps.instruction: Pick exactly 30 L4‑stage worms onto each 6 cm NGM/OP50 plate and prepare three replicate plates for each strain to be tested.

steps.title: Heat‑shock plates at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Place all assay plates in a 37 °C incubator for 2 hours, arranging them in a single layer and avoiding stacking.

steps.title: Recover plates for 30 min then incubate
steps.instruction: Remove plates from the incubator, lay them in a single layer on the bench top for a 30‑minute recovery, then stack the plates in a box and incubate at 20 °C.

steps.title: Score worm survival after 24 h
steps.instruction: After 24 hours at 20 °C, assess each worm for alive/dead status; if a worm is not moving, test its response by tapping with a worm pick and/or check for pharyngeal pumping.
